questions.q: What is measurement?
questions.a: Comparing an unknown quantity with a fixed known quantity (unit) - a number with a unit.

questions.q: Why do we need standard units?
questions.a: Hand-span or pace differ person to person; standard units give the same result everywhere.

questions.q: Name the standard unit of length.
questions.a: The metre (m) of the SI system.

questions.q: State the units of length with their relations.
Which unit suits measuring the length of a pencil? Why?
questions.a: Centimetre - the pencil is a few times 10 cm, easy to read on a scale.

questions.q: Which unit would you use for the distance between two cities?
questions.a: Kilometre - such distances are too large for metres.

What is rectilinear motion?
questions.a: Motion along a straight line - a car on a straight road, a falling stone.

questions.q: Give two examples of rectilinear motion.
questions.a: A ball dropped from height and a train on a straight track.

questions.q: How is rectilinear motion different from circular motion?
questions.a: Straight-line path versus a circular path around a centre.

questions.q: What is circular motion?
questions.a: Motion of an object around a fixed centre at constant distance - a fan blade, a clock hand.

questions.q: Give two examples of circular motion.
questions.a: A potter's wheel and the tip of a moving clock's minute hand.

questions.q: Is every point of a rotating fan in circular motion?
questions.a: Yes - each point moves in its own circle around the axle.

questions.q: What is periodic motion?
questions.a: Motion that repeats itself after fixed intervals - a pendulum, a swing.

questions.q: Give two examples of periodic motion.
questions.a: A pendulum's swing and a drum's vibrating membrane.

questions.q: How is periodic motion useful to us?
questions.a: Its regularity measures time - clocks use oscillations (pendulum, quartz).
